steps.title: Let the three consecutive even
steps.body:
Let the three consecutive even numbers be
\[
2n-2,\quad 2n,\quad 2n+2
\]

steps.title: The difference between the square
steps.body:
The difference between the square of the largest and the square of the smallest is
\[
(2n+2)^2-(2n-2)^2
\]

\[
=(4n^2+8n+4)-(4n^2-8n+4)
\]

\[
=16n
\]

steps.title: Since , the result is
steps.body: Since \(8\times\text{middle number}=8(2n)=16n\), the result is 8 times the middle number.

all::May2021_P1H__Q17__p15-15__m03__Alge.finalAnswer: The difference is always 8 times the middle number.

steps.title: For the circle with centre
steps.body:
For the circle with centre \(O\):

\[
\angle AOB=50^\circ,\qquad OA=OB=5
\]

steps.title: For the circle with centre
steps.body:
For the circle with centre \(P\), let

\[
\angle APB=\theta
\]

steps.title: The common region is made
steps.body: The common region is made from two minor segments.

steps.title: For the circle with centre
steps.body:
For the circle with centre \(O\):

\[
\text{segment area}
=\frac{50}{360}\pi(5)^2-\frac{1}{2}(5)^2\sin 50^\circ
=1.3328\ldots
\]

steps.title: For the circle with centre
steps.body:
For the circle with centre \(P\):

\[
\text{segment area}
=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi(4)^2-\frac{1}{2}(4)^2\sin \theta
\]

\[
=1.7284\ldots
\]

steps.title: The triangular end is isosceles,
steps.body:
The triangular end is isosceles, with

\[
AC=BC=12,\qquad AB=10
\]

steps.title: The perpendicular height of the
steps.body:
The perpendicular height of the triangle is found by halving \(AB\):

\[
AM=5
\]

\[
CM^2=12^2-5^2=144-25=119
\]

\[
CM=\sqrt{119}
\]

steps.title: The projection of on the
steps.body:
The projection of \(AD\) on the horizontal base goes from \(A\) to the midpoint of \(FE\). Its length is

\[
\sqrt{15^2+5^2}=\sqrt{250}
\]

steps.title: So, for the angle between
steps.body:
So, for the angle \(\theta\) between \(AD\) and the base,

\[
\tan \theta=\frac{\sqrt{119}}{\sqrt{250}}
\]

\[
\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{119}}{\sqrt{250}}\right)=34.602\ldots
\]

steps.title: Since lies on , let
steps.body:
Since \(P\) lies on \(OC\), let

\[
\overrightarrow{OP}=t(2\mathbf a+3\mathbf b)
\]

steps.title: So
steps.body:
So

\[
\overrightarrow{OP}
=2\mathbf a+s(5\mathbf b-2\mathbf a)
\]

\[
\overrightarrow{OP}
=(2-2s)\mathbf a+5s\mathbf b
\]

steps.title: Compare this with
steps.body:
Compare this with

\[
t(2\mathbf a+3\mathbf b)=2t\mathbf a+3t\mathbf b
\]
